company.name: Coalesce.io
company.industry: Data transformation SaaS for the Snowflake ecosystem

routing_rationale: Operational security-and-compliance owner. Self-described 'Multi-Cloud | Security + Compliance | SOC 2'. 7+ years compliance-heavy infra (Roivant pharma, ComplySci financial-regulatory SaaS). Hiring manager for Senior DevOps EMEA role. Distinct angle: continuous reconciliation between Terraform-declared state and actual deployed state, in his vocabulary (diff, before drift compounds).

research_summary.trigger_event: Two acquired stacks (CastorDoc March 2025, SYNQ March 2026) absorbed in twelve months expand the IaC-to-cloud surface his team must declare and continuously verify.
research_summary.key_insight: Justin reads SOC 2 vocabulary natively — explaining is fatal. Generalized 'multi-cloud Kubernetes at scale' rather than quoting the public job spec's '20+ Kubernetes deployments across three clouds' to keep observation observational rather than surveillance-y. The CTA's binary technical choice ('Terraform-only, or runtime checks on top?') invites him to share his stack — implicit category-incumbent positioning lives there rather than as an explicit additive-clause.

draft.body:
Two acquired stacks absorbed in twelve months, multi-cloud Kubernetes at scale, the same small infra team — the gap between what Terraform declares and what's actually deployed widens between audit cycles in ways that aren't visible until they accumulate.

Transilience surfaces this diff continuously — Terraform-declared vs. actual deployed state — before drift compounds.

How does your team currently handle drift detection across the acquired stacks — Terraform-only, or runtime checks on top?
draft.architecture: signal-to-question — three structural facts triangulate into the named drift problem; CTA is a real engineering question with a binary technical choice

verdict_history.reason: 'Quarterly audit cadence' imprecise — SOC 2 Type 2 is annual; Justin would catch the wobble.
Audit-cadence fix correct, CTA was opaque consultantese AND a meeting-ask the four sentences hadn't earned.
User-level review caught: same four-item product line as Satish/Mike, 'after' subject pattern echoing across three drafts.

Cross-draft witness flagged: 'effective cloud state' was vendor vocab where subject said 'actual'; 'audit findings' framed value in audit terms when practitioner concern is operational drift; 'additive to existing CSPM and observability' echoed Satish's 'additive to existing CSPM'; 'Transilience runs' opener structure echoed Satish's inversion.
'Across the surface' was filler; 'additive' echo with Satish unresolved.

Cut filler, dropped additive sentence (CTA implicitly handles category positioning), restructured product sentence to subject-verb-object (distinct from Satish's inversion). Three sentences, all earning their place.

witness.what_works: Subject is flat technical and drops the 'after' pattern. 'Diff' is engineer vocabulary. 'Before drift compounds' is operational, not audit-framed. CTA's binary technical choice invites him to share his stack, which implicitly handles the CSPM-incumbent positioning. Three sentences — appropriate for a brevity practitioner.
witness.what_fails: The CSPM-incumbent preemption is no longer explicit. Acceptable risk because the IaC-declared-vs-actual-deployed framing is itself the differentiator (most CSPMs check cloud config, not Terraform reconciliation), and Justin's seven years of compliance-stack fluency means he'll do the category positioning himself if the substance is right.
